content.text:
These are the parts of the **training program**. You never run them one by one: the Colab notebook (`notebooks/train_colab.ipynb`) calls them in the right order.

## How they work together
```
zip from the app ─► data.py ─► review.py ─► train.py ─► export_onnx.py ─► verify_onnx.py ─► .onnx file for the app
 (or synthetic.py)  (load)     (fix labels)  (uses model.py)  (convert)        (final check)
                              config.py = shared rules used by all files
```

## What each file does

| File | What it's for |
|---|---|
| `__init__.py` | Empty on purpose. It tells Python that `src` is a package, so the notebook can write `from src import data`. |
| `config.py` | **The shared rules between this project and the app.** The 3 classes in order (`empty`, `filled`, `erased`), the image size (32×32) and the ONNX version (opset 11). If you change anything here, the app code must change too. |
| `data.py` | **Loads the data.** It unzips the files exported from the app, reads each file name (scan ID, template, question, option) and applies your label fixes from `labels_override.csv`. It then splits the data into train / validation / test **by scan** and prepares each image exactly like the app does (resize to 32×32, divide by 255). During training, it also changes images randomly (light, blur, small shifts) so the model can handle different photos. |
| `model.py` | **The model itself (BubbleNet).** A very small neural network: 3 layers that look at the image, plus 1 layer that decides empty / filled / erased. About 27,000 numbers in total, around 100 KB. It only uses operations that the app's OpenCV 4.5.3 can run. |
| `train.py` | **Trains the model.** It learns from the training images, checks itself on the validation images after each round, and keeps the best version. Then it prints a report: accuracy, a table of mistakes, and **how many cells the new model gets wrong compared with the old 50% rule**. It can also save and load the model (`.pt` file). |
| `review.py` | **Your label-fixing tools in Colab.** It shows grids of cell images with numbers so you can fix labels with one line, for example `rv.fix("filled", [3, 17], to="erased")`. `rv.ignore_sheet(...)` removes a bad scan. After training, `rv.show_suspicious()` shows the cells where the model disagrees with the label, which are often your labeling mistakes. |
| `export_onnx.py` | **Converts the trained model into an `.onnx` file** the Android app can load. It has 2 ways to convert: the PyTorch exporter, and a backup that builds the file by hand if PyTorch removes the old exporter. It also saves test samples for checking and writes `model_card.json` (version, accuracy, date). |
| `verify_onnx.py` | **The final safety check.** It runs the `.onnx` file with **exactly OpenCV 4.5.3**, the same version as in your app, in a separate Python 3.9 environment. It checks that the results match what PyTorch gave. If it prints **"OK"**, the model will work in the app. |
| `synthetic.py` | **Makes fake training data** in the same format as the app's export: drawn bubbles that are filled, empty, erased or crossed out. It's only for practicing the notebook when you have no real data. **Never use a model trained on fake data in the app.** |

## Which notebook section uses which file
- Sections **2–3** (load data, fix labels): `data.py` + `review.py`
- Section **4** (train): `train.py` + `model.py`
- Section **5** (suspicious cells): `review.py`
- Section **6** (export and check): `export_onnx.py` + `verify_onnx.py`

# QuizMark — Train model phân loại ô tô (trống / tô / tẩy)

Chạy **lần lượt từng ô từ trên xuống** (bấm ▶ hoặc `Shift + Enter`).

**Trước khi chạy lần đầu:**
1. **Runtime → Change runtime type**: chọn GPU nếu muốn (không bắt buộc — model rất nhỏ, CPU cũng chỉ vài phút).
2. Repo GitHub để **private** → bấm biểu tượng 🔑 **Secrets** ở thanh bên trái → **Add new secret**:
   tên `GITHUB_TOKEN`, giá trị là token GitHub chỉ đọc → bật **Notebook access**.
3. Các file `bubble_dataset_*.zip` xuất từ app phải nằm trong `My Drive/quizmark-ml/data/`.
   Chưa có dữ liệu thật? Đặt `USE_SYNTHETIC = True` để chạy thử toàn bộ bằng dữ liệu giả.

**Vòng lặp làm việc:** 2. Nạp dữ liệu → 3. Sửa nhãn → 4. Train → 5. Xem mẫu đáng ngờ → sửa → train lại (1–2 vòng) → 6. Export → 7. Lưu.

# ===== CẤU HÌNH — sửa nếu cần =====
GITHUB_REPO   = "HuongNguyenQuoc/quizmark-ml"   # repo GitHub của bạn (public, không cần token)
DRIVE_ROOT    = "/content/drive/MyDrive/quizmark-ml"

## 1. Cài đặt

except Exception:

## 3. Kiểm tra & sửa nhãn

Nhãn ban đầu lấy theo ngưỡng 50% cũ của app nên có chỗ sai. Việc của bạn:
- **Ô đã tẩy / gạch chéo** đang nằm trong `filled` hoặc `empty` → đổi thành `erased`.
- **Ô tô nhạt** bị nằm trong `empty` → đổi thành `filled`.
- **Lần quét bị lỗi** (nhận sai góc phiếu, ảnh ô toàn chữ in) → bỏ cả lần quét.

content.text:
Yes. The next step is training data, and I can make it for you on the computer. One thing to be clear about first:

- **A model trained only on computer-made images is a practice model ("v0").** It will learn my drawn marks, not real pencil on paper. Its accuracy score will look high, but that doesn't prove it works on real sheets.
- It's still useful now: you can train a model with many correct labels, put it in the app (step B3), and test the whole system on your phone. Later, real sheets make it reliable.

So I'll build a generator that makes **many realistic sheet photos** and cuts the cells with **exactly the same steps as the app**. It also writes the **correct label for every cell**, including "erased", so you don't need to label by hand. I'll make the marks and photo effects more realistic than before.

"""Make a COMPUTER-MADE training dataset in exactly the format the QuizMark app exports.

Steps for every sheet:
  1. Render a template PDF from the app (QuizMark/app/src/main/res/raw/form_*.pdf).
  2. Draw marks exactly on the cells the app reads (ROI coordinates copied from the app's
     util/scanner/*Processor.kt, mapped through the same 4 corner markers ScannerCore uses).
     Mark styles: dark / light / partial / overflowing pencil, pen, erased, X, single slash.
  3. Add photo effects: desk border, perspective, uneven light, shadow, colour tint, blur,
     noise, lower resolution, JPEG compression.
  4. Run a Python copy of the app pipeline (corner detection → 800x1200 warp → adaptive
     threshold → 50% rule) and cut every cell from the warped gray image, like BubbleDatasetDumper.

Outputs (in --out):
  bubble_dataset_synth_<tag>.zip  → upload to  My Drive/quizmark-ml/data/
  labels_override.csv             → upload to  My Drive/quizmark-ml/   (TRUE labels incl. "erased")
  photos/                         → a few sample sheet photos to look at
  stats.txt                       → what the old 50% rule gets wrong on this data

This is practice data. A model trained only on it must not be shipped before it is trained on real sheets.

Usage (needs: numpy, opencv-python, pymupdf):
  python tools/make_sheet_dataset.py --out ../quizmark-synthetic --per-template 12 --seed 2026
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import io
import zipfile
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

import cv2
import fitz  # pymupdf
import numpy as np

DEFAULT_RAW = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "QuizMark" / "app" / "src" / "main" / "res" / "raw"
W, H = 800.0, 1200.0
FILLED_STYLES = ("dark", "light", "partial", "overflow", "pen")
ERASED_STYLES = ("erased", "x", "slash")


# ---------------- Layouts copied from the app's processors (800x1200 warped space) ----------------
def _basic(sbd, code, cols):
    specs = [dict(kind="grid", region="sbd", roi=sbd, rows=10, cols=6, r=0.38),
             dict(kind="grid", region="code", roi=code, rows=10, cols=3, r=0.38)]
    specs += [dict(kind="answers", region="ans", roi=(x, y, w, h), rows=e - s + 1, cols=4, start=s, r=0.36)
              for x, y, w, h, s, e in cols]
    return specs


LAYOUTS = {
    2: ("form_20_cau", _basic((186, 337, 201, 381), (417, 338, 104, 382),
                              [(221, 759, 131, 380, 1, 10), (418, 760, 131, 380, 11, 20)])),
    3: ("form_40_cau", _basic((90, 337, 198, 384), (320, 337, 100, 384),
                              [(520, 337, 130, 384, 1, 10), (123, 757, 130, 386, 11, 20),
                               (321, 757, 130, 386, 21, 30), (520, 757, 130, 386, 31, 40)])),
    4: ("form_50_cau", _basic((601, 80, 107, 254), (730, 80, 54, 254),
                              [(128, 445, 233, 717, 1, 25), (495, 445, 233, 717, 26, 50)])),
    5: ("form_120_cau", _basic((601, 78, 107, 254), (731, 78, 55, 254),
                               [(61, 389, 129, 779, 1, 30), (257, 389, 129, 779, 31, 60),
                                (448, 389, 129, 779, 61, 90), (642, 389, 129, 779, 91, 120)])),
    1: ("form_thpt_2025",
        [dict(kind="grid", region="sbd", roi=(549, 84, 138, 253), rows=10, cols=8, r=0.4),
         dict(kind="grid", region="code", roi=(713, 84, 70, 253), rows=10, cols=4, r=0.4)]
        + [dict(kind="answers", region="p1", roi=(x, 435, 147, 197), rows=10, cols=4, start=s, r=0.4)
           for x, s in ((53, 1), (241, 11), (428, 21), (615, 31))]
        + [dict(kind="tf", region="p2", roi=(x, 719, 68, 79), rows=4, cols=2, start=41 + 4 * i, r=0.36)
           for i, x in enumerate((55, 132, 244, 319, 430, 505, 618, 693))]
        + [dict(kind="number", region="p3", roi=(x, 894, 101, 244), rows=12, cols=4, start=73 + i, r=0.36)
           for i, x in enumerate((53, 173, 293, 412, 533, 653))]),
}


def p3_valid(r: int, c: int) -> bool:
    """Same rule as ExamThptProcessor.readPart3Box: row 0 only col 0 ('-'), row 1 cols 1-2 ('.')."""
    return c == 0 if r == 0 else (c in (1, 2) if r == 1 else True)


def cell_name_parts(spec, r, c):
    """(region, position, option) exactly as the app's BubbleDatasetDumper names files."""
    kind = spec["kind"]
    if kind == "grid":
        return spec["region"], f"c{c}", str(r)
    if kind == "answers":
        return spec["region"], f"q{spec['start'] + r}", "ABCD"[c]
    if kind == "tf":
        return "p2", f"q{spec['start'] + r}", "T" if c == 0 else "F"
    option = "neg" if r == 0 else ("dot" if r == 1 else str(r - 2))
    return "p3", f"q{spec['start']}c{c}", option


def cells_of(spec):
    for r in range(spec["rows"]):
        for c in range(spec["cols"]):
            if spec["kind"] != "number" or p3_valid(r, c):
                yield r, c


# ---------------- Same corner detection as ScannerCore.findExamCorners ----------------
def find_corners(gray):
    edges = cv2.Canny(cv2.GaussianBlur(gray, (5, 5), 0), 75, 200)
    contours, _ = cv2.findContours(edges, cv2.RETR_LIST, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
    squares = []
    for cnt in contours:
        approx = cv2.approxPolyDP(cnt.astype(np.float32), 0.03 * cv2.arcLength(cnt, True), True)
        if 4 <= len(approx) <= 6:
            area = cv2.contourArea(approx)
            if 100 <= area <= 30000:
                x, y, w, h = cv2.boundingRect(cnt)
                if 0.5 <= w / h <= 2.0:
                    squares.append((approx, area))
    if len(squares) < 4:
        return None
    median = sorted(a for _, a in squares)[len(squares) // 2]
    centers = []
    for s, a in squares:
        if median * 0.1 <= a <= median * 15:
            x, y, w, h = cv2.boundingRect(s.astype(np.int32))
            centers.append((x + w / 2, y + h / 2))
    if len(centers) < 4:
        return None
    c = np.array(centers)
    tl, br = c[np.argmin(c.sum(1))], c[np.argmax(c.sum(1))]
    tr, bl = c[np.argmax(c[:, 0] - c[:, 1])], c[np.argmin(c[:, 0] - c[:, 1])]
    wt, hl = np.linalg.norm(tr - tl), np.linalg.norm(bl - tl)
    wb, hr = np.linalg.norm(br - bl), np.linalg.norm(br - tr)
    if wt < 80 or hl < 100 or hl < wt * 1.05 or abs(wt - wb) > wt * 0.25 or abs(hl - hr) > hl * 0.25:
        return None
    return np.array([tl, tr, br, bl], dtype=np.float32)


# ---------------- Drawing marks ----------------
def _blob_mask(shape, center, radius, rng, roughness=0.12):
    """Irregular filled shape (hand-made fill), radius varies around the circle."""
    angles = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 40, endpoint=False)
    radii = radius * (1 + rng.normal(0, roughness, angles.size))
    radii = cv2.GaussianBlur(radii.reshape(1, -1).astype(np.float32), (1, 5), 0).ravel()
    pts = np.stack([center[0] + radii * np.cos(angles), center[1] + radii * np.sin(angles)], 1)
    mask = np.zeros(shape, np.uint8)
    cv2.fillPoly(mask, [pts.astype(np.int32)], 255, cv2.LINE_AA)
    return mask


def _paint(img, mask, tone, rng, grain):
    """Darken img towards `tone` where mask is set, with graphite grain texture."""
    m = mask.astype(np.float32) / 255.0
    texture = tone + rng.normal(0, grain, img.shape)
    texture = cv2.GaussianBlur(texture.astype(np.float32), (3, 3), 0)
    out = img.astype(np.float32) * (1 - m) + np.minimum(img.astype(np.float32), texture) * m
    img[:] = np.clip(out, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)


def _strokes(img, center, radius, rng, tone, n, thickness):
    for _ in range(n):
        ang = rng.uniform(0, np.pi)
        off = rng.uniform(-0.6, 0.6) * radius
        dx, dy = np.cos(ang) * radius, np.sin(ang) * radius
        ox, oy = -np.sin(ang) * off, np.cos(ang) * off
        p1 = (int(center[0] - dx + ox), int(center[1] - dy + oy))
        p2 = (int(center[0] + dx + ox), int(center[1] + dy + oy))
        cv2.line(img, p1, p2, float(tone), thickness, cv2.LINE_AA)


def draw_mark(img, center, radius, style, rng):
    cx, cy = center
    jitter = rng.normal(0, radius * 0.08, 2)
    c = (cx + jitter[0], cy + jitter[1])
    if style == "dark":
        _paint(img, _blob_mask(img.shape, c, radius * rng.uniform(0.82, 1.0), rng), rng.uniform(20, 75), rng, 18)
    elif style == "light":
        _paint(img, _blob_mask(img.shape, c, radius * rng.uniform(0.8, 1.0), rng), rng.uniform(105, 165), rng, 22)
    elif style == "partial":   # half-filled, crescent or small dot
        sub = rng.choice(["small", "crescent"])
        if sub == "small":
            mask = _blob_mask(img.shape, c, radius * rng.uniform(0.4, 0.65), rng, 0.15)
        else:
            mask = _blob_mask(img.shape, c, radius * 0.95, rng)
            off = rng.uniform(0.35, 0.7) * radius
            ang = rng.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi)
            cut = _blob_mask(img.shape, (c[0] + off * np.cos(ang), c[1] + off * np.sin(ang)), radius * 0.9, rng)
            mask = cv2.subtract(mask, cut)
        _paint(img, mask, rng.uniform(25, 90), rng, 18)
    elif style == "overflow":  # bigger than the bubble and off-centre
        c2 = (c[0] + rng.uniform(-0.25, 0.25) * radius, c[1] + rng.uniform(-0.25, 0.25) * radius)
        _paint(img, _blob_mask(img.shape, c2, radius * rng.uniform(1.05, 1.3), rng, 0.15), rng.uniform(25, 80), rng, 18)
    elif style == "pen":       # ballpoint: dark, smooth, scribble strokes
        _paint(img, _blob_mask(img.shape, c, radius * rng.uniform(0.8, 0.98), rng, 0.08), rng.uniform(10, 45), rng, 6)
        _strokes(img, c, radius * 0.9, rng, rng.uniform(5, 30), int(rng.integers(2, 5)), 1)
    elif style == "erased":    # graphite left after erasing + eraser streaks
        _paint(img, _blob_mask(img.shape, c, radius * rng.uniform(0.8, 1.05), rng, 0.2), rng.uniform(165, 215), rng, 15)
        _strokes(img, c, radius, rng, rng.uniform(140, 200), int(rng.integers(1, 4)), 1)
    elif style == "x":
        tone, d = rng.uniform(20, 90), radius * rng.uniform(0.7, 1.05)
        t = int(rng.integers(1, 3))
        cv2.line(img, (int(c[0] - d), int(c[1] - d)), (int(c[0] + d), int(c[1] + d)), float(tone), t, cv2.LINE_AA)
        cv2.line(img, (int(c[0] - d), int(c[1] + d)), (int(c[0] + d), int(c[1] - d)), float(tone), t, cv2.LINE_AA)
    elif style == "slash":     # crossed out with one line
        tone, d = rng.uniform(20, 90), radius * rng.uniform(0.8, 1.15)
        ang = rng.uniform(0.5, 1.1)
        cv2.line(img, (int(c[0] - d * np.cos(ang)), int(c[1] + d * np.sin(ang))),
                 (int(c[0] + d * np.cos(ang)), int(c[1] - d * np.sin(ang))), float(tone), int(rng.integers(1, 3)), cv2.LINE_AA)


def filled_style(rng):
    return rng.choice(FILLED_STYLES, p=[0.55, 0.13, 0.12, 0.08, 0.12])


def erased_style(rng):
    return rng.choice(ERASED_STYLES, p=[0.6, 0.25, 0.15])


def plan_marks(layout, template_id, rng):
    """{(spec_index, r, c): style}. Includes realistic mistakes: blanks, double fills, changed answers."""
    marks = {}
    for i, spec in enumerate(layout):
        kind, rows, cols = spec["kind"], spec["rows"], spec["cols"]
        if kind == "grid":  # one digit per column
            for c in range(cols):
                marks[(i, int(rng.integers(rows)), c)] = filled_style(rng) if rng.random() < 0.97 else erased_style(rng)
                if rng.random() < 0.06:  # changed a digit
                    marks.setdefault((i, int(rng.integers(rows)), c), erased_style(rng))
        elif kind in ("answers", "tf"):
            for r in range(rows):
                u = rng.random()
                chosen = [] if u < 0.07 else (list(rng.choice(cols, 2, replace=False)) if u < 0.11
                                              else [int(rng.integers(cols))])
                for c in chosen:
                    marks[(i, r, int(c))] = filled_style(rng)
                if rng.random() < 0.22:  # changed mind on another option
                    others = [c for c in range(cols) if c not in chosen]
                    if others:
                        marks[(i, r, int(rng.choice(others)))] = erased_style(rng)
        else:  # THPT part 3 number: optional sign/decimal point + digits from the left
            n_digits = int(rng.integers(1, 5))
            for c in range(n_digits):
                marks[(i, 2 + int(rng.integers(10)), c)] = filled_style(rng)
            if rng.random() < 0.2:
                marks[(i, 0, 0)] = filled_style(rng)
            if rng.random() < 0.25:
                marks[(i, 1, int(rng.choice([1, 2])))] = filled_style(rng)
            if rng.random() < 0.2:
                r, c = 2 + int(rng.integers(10)), int(rng.integers(4))
                marks.setdefault((i, r, c), erased_style(rng))
    return marks


# ---------------- Photo effects ----------------
def make_photo(page_gray, rng):
    h, w = page_gray.shape
    pad = int(w * rng.uniform(0.05, 0.12))
    desk = np.array([rng.uniform(40, 120), rng.uniform(60, 140), rng.uniform(80, 170)], np.float32)
    canvas = np.empty((h + 2 * pad, w + 2 * pad, 3), np.float32)
    canvas[:] = desk + rng.normal(0, 6, canvas.shape)
    canvas[pad:pad + h, pad:pad + w] = cv2.cvtColor(page_gray, cv2.COLOR_GRAY2BGR)
    H2, W2 = canvas.shape[:2]
    src = np.float32([[0, 0], [W2, 0], [W2, H2], [0, H2]])
    dst = (src + rng.uniform(-0.03, 0.03, src.shape) * [W2, H2]).astype(np.float32)
    canvas = cv2.warpPerspective(canvas, cv2.getPerspectiveTransform(src, dst), (W2, H2), borderMode=cv2.BORDER_REPLICATE)
    # uneven light + colour tint (warm lamp / cool daylight)
    gx = np.linspace(rng.uniform(0.75, 1.0), rng.uniform(0.9, 1.1), W2, dtype=np.float32)[None, :, None]
    gy = np.linspace(rng.uniform(0.85, 1.08), rng.uniform(0.75, 1.0), H2, dtype=np.float32)[:, None, None]
    tint = np.array([rng.uniform(0.85, 1.05), rng.uniform(0.95, 1.03), rng.uniform(0.97, 1.12)], np.float32)
    canvas = canvas * gx * gy * tint
    if rng.random() < 0.5:  # soft shadow (hand / phone)
        mask = np.zeros((H2, W2), np.float32)
        cv2.ellipse(mask, (int(rng.uniform(0, W2)), int(rng.uniform(0, H2))),
                    (int(W2 * rng.uniform(0.2, 0.5)), int(H2 * rng.uniform(0.15, 0.4))), rng.uniform(0, 180), 0, 360, 1, -1)
        mask = cv2.GaussianBlur(mask, (0, 0), W2 * 0.06)
        canvas *= (1 - rng.uniform(0.15, 0.4) * mask)[:, :, None]
    canvas += rng.normal(0, rng.uniform(1.5, 5), canvas.shape)
    photo = np.clip(canvas, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    blur = rng.choice(["none", "gauss", "motion"], p=[0.4, 0.4, 0.2])
    if blur == "gauss":
        photo = cv2.GaussianBlur(photo, (0, 0), rng.uniform(0.6, 1.4))
    elif blur == "motion":
        k = int(rng.integers(3, 6))
        kernel = np.zeros((k, k), np.float32)
        kernel[k // 2, :] = 1.0 / k
        rot = cv2.getRotationMatrix2D((k / 2 - 0.5, k / 2 - 0.5), rng.uniform(0, 180), 1)
        photo = cv2.filter2D(photo, -1, cv2.warpAffine(kernel, rot, (k, k)))
    scale = rng.uniform(0.7, 1.0)  # lower camera resolution
    if scale < 0.98:
        photo = cv2.resize(photo, None, fx=scale, fy=scale, interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
    ok, buf = cv2.imencode(".jpg", photo, [cv2.IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY, int(rng.integers(60, 95))])
    return cv2.imdecode(buf, cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)


# ---------------- Python copy of the app pipeline ----------------
def app_gray(photo_bgr):
    """App: bitmapToMat gives RGBA, then COLOR_BGR2GRAY → R and B weights are swapped. Do the same."""
    return cv2.cvtColor(cv2.cvtColor(photo_bgr, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB), cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)


def run_app_pipeline(photo_bgr, layout):
    gray = app_gray(photo_bgr)
    corners = find_corners(gray)
    if corners is None:
        return None
    m = cv2.getPerspectiveTransform(corners, np.float32([[0, 0], [W, 0], [W, H], [0, H]]))
    warped = cv2.warpPerspective(gray, m, (int(W), int(H)))
    binary = cv2.adaptiveThreshold(warped, 255, cv2.ADAPTIVE_THRESH_GAUSSIAN_C, cv2.THRESH_BINARY_INV, 51, 10)
    cells = []
    for i, spec in enumerate(layout):
        x, y, w, h = spec["roi"]
        cw, ch = w / spec["cols"], h / spec["rows"]
        radius = int(min(cw, ch) * spec["r"])
        mask = np.zeros((int(ch), int(cw)), np.uint8)
        cv2.circle(mask, (int(round(cw / 2)), int(round(ch / 2))), radius, 255, -1)
        for r, c in cells_of(spec):
            rx, ry = x + int(c * cw), y + int(r * ch)
            cell_bin = binary[ry:ry + int(ch), rx:rx + int(cw)]
            filled = cv2.countNonZero(cv2.bitwise_and(cell_bin, mask[:cell_bin.shape[0], :cell_bin.shape[1]])) \
                > np.pi * radius * radius * 0.5
            cells.append((i, r, c, filled, warped[ry:ry + int(ch), rx:rx + int(cw)].copy()))
    return cells


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--raw", default=str(DEFAULT_RAW), help="folder with the app's form_*.pdf templates")
    ap.add_argument("--per-template", type=int, default=12)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=2026)
    ap.add_argument("--tag", default="v1")
    ap.add_argument("--sample-photos", type=int, default=1, help="photos to keep per template for viewing")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    rng = np.random.default_rng(args.seed)
    out = Path(args.out)
    (out / "photos").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    zip_path = out / f"bubble_dataset_synth_{args.tag}.zip"
    labels, stats, skipped = {}, Counter(), 0

    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, "w", zipfile.ZIP_STORED) as zf:  # PNGs are already compressed
        for template_id, (stem, layout) in sorted(LAYOUTS.items()):
            pix = fitz.open(Path(args.raw) / f"{stem}.pdf")[0].get_pixmap(dpi=200)
            base = np.frombuffer(pix.samples, np.uint8).reshape(pix.height, pix.width, pix.n)
            base = cv2.cvtColor(base, cv2.COLOR_RGB2GRAY if pix.n == 3 else cv2.COLOR_RGBA2GRAY)
            corners = find_corners(base)
            to_page = cv2.getPerspectiveTransform(np.float32([[0, 0], [W, 0], [W, H], [0, H]]), corners)
            scale = np.linalg.norm(corners[1] - corners[0]) / W

            for n in range(args.per_template):
                page = base.copy()
                marks = plan_marks(layout, template_id, rng)
                for (i, r, c), style in marks.items():
                    spec = layout[i]
                    x, y, w, h = spec["roi"]
                    cw, ch = w / spec["cols"], h / spec["rows"]
                    wx, wy = x + (c + 0.5) * cw, y + (r + 0.5) * ch
                    px, py = cv2.perspectiveTransform(np.float32([[[wx, wy]]]), to_page)[0, 0]
                    draw_mark(page, (px, py), min(cw, ch) * spec["r"] * scale, style, rng)
                photo = make_photo(page, rng)
                cells = run_app_pipeline(photo, layout)
                if cells is None:
                    skipped += 1
                    continue
                if n < args.sample_photos:
                    cv2.imwrite(str(out / "photos" / f"synth_t{template_id}_{stem[5:]}_{n + 1}.jpg"), photo)
                sheet_id = f"990101-{template_id}{n:05d}-syn{args.seed % 1000:03d}"
                for i, r, c, filled, crop in cells:
                    region, position, option = cell_name_parts(layout[i], r, c)
                    name = f"{sheet_id}_t{template_id}_{region}_{position}_{option}.png"
                    auto = "filled" if filled else "empty"
                    style = marks.get((i, r, c))
                    truth = "empty" if style is None else ("erased" if style in ERASED_STYLES else "filled")
                    zf.writestr(f"bubble_dataset/{auto}/{name}", cv2.imencode(".png", crop)[1].tobytes())
                    labels[name] = truth
                    stats[(truth, auto)] += 1
                    if style:
                        stats[("style", style, auto)] += 1

    with (out / "labels_override.csv").open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f)
        writer.writerow(["filename", "label"])
        writer.writerows(sorted(labels.items()))

    total = sum(v for k, v in stats.items() if k[0] != "style")
    lines = [f"Sheets: {args.per_template * len(LAYOUTS) - skipped} made, {skipped} skipped (app could not find corners)",
             f"Cells: {total}"]
    for truth in ("empty", "filled", "erased"):
        n_all = stats[(truth, "empty")] + stats[(truth, "filled")]
        wrong = stats[(truth, "empty")] if truth == "filled" else stats[(truth, "filled")]
        lines.append(f"  {truth:>6}: {n_all:6d} cells — old 50% rule wrong on {wrong} ({wrong / max(n_all, 1):.1%})")
    lines.append("Old rule by mark style (cells read as 'filled' / total):")
    for style in FILLED_STYLES + ERASED_STYLES:
        f_, e_ = stats[("style", style, "filled")], stats[("style", style, "empty")]
        lines.append(f"  {style:>8}: {f_}/{f_ + e_}")
    report = "\n".join(lines)
    (out / "stats.txt").write_text(report + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(report)
    print(f"\nWrote {zip_path} ({zip_path.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB) and {out / 'labels_override.csv'}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Make a COMPUTER-MADE training dataset in exactly the format the QuizMark app exports.

Steps for every sheet:
  1. Render a template PDF from the app (QuizMark/app/src/main/res/raw/form_*.pdf).
  2. Draw marks exactly on the cells the app reads (ROI coordinates copied from the app's
     util/scanner/*Processor.kt, mapped through the same 4 corner markers ScannerCore uses).
     Mark styles: dark / light / partial / overflowing pencil, pen, erased, X, single slash.
  3. Add photo effects: desk border, perspective, uneven light, shadow, colour tint, blur,
     noise, lower resolution, JPEG compression.
  4. Run a Python copy of the app pipeline (corner detection → 800x1200 warp → adaptive
     threshold → 50% rule) and cut every cell from the warped gray image, like BubbleDatasetDumper.

Outputs (in --out):
  bubble_dataset_synth_<tag>.zip  → upload to  My Drive/quizmark-ml/data/
  labels_override.csv             → upload to  My Drive/quizmark-ml/   (TRUE labels incl. "erased")
  photos/                         → a few sample sheet photos to look at
  stats.txt                       → what the old 50% rule gets wrong on this data

This is practice data. A model trained only on it must not be shipped before it is trained on real sheets.

Usage (needs: numpy, opencv-python, pymupdf):
  python tools/make_sheet_dataset.py --out ../quizmark-synthetic --per-template 12 --seed 2026
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import io
import zipfile
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

import cv2
import fitz  # pymupdf
import numpy as np

DEFAULT_RAW = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "QuizMark" / "app" / "src" / "main" / "res" / "raw"
W, H = 800.0, 1200.0
FILLED_STYLES = ("dark", "light", "partial", "overflow", "pen")
ERASED_STYLES = ("erased", "x", "slash")


# ---------------- Layouts copied from the app's processors (800x1200 warped space) ----------------
def _basic(sbd, code, cols):
    specs = [dict(kind="grid", region="sbd", roi=sbd, rows=10, cols=6, r=0.38),
             dict(kind="grid", region="code", roi=code, rows=10, cols=3, r=0.38)]
    specs += [dict(kind="answers", region="ans", roi=(x, y, w, h), rows=e - s + 1, cols=4, start=s, r=0.36)
              for x, y, w, h, s, e in cols]
    return specs


LAYOUTS = {
    2: ("form_20_cau", _basic((186, 337, 201, 381), (417, 338, 104, 382),
                              [(221, 759, 131, 380, 1, 10), (418, 760, 131, 380, 11, 20)])),
    3: ("form_40_cau", _basic((90, 337, 198, 384), (320, 337, 100, 384),
                              [(520, 337, 130, 384, 1, 10), (123, 757, 130, 386, 11, 20),
                               (321, 757, 130, 386, 21, 30), (520, 757, 130, 386, 31, 40)])),
    4: ("form_50_cau", _basic((601, 80, 107, 254), (730, 80, 54, 254),
                              [(128, 445, 233, 717, 1, 25), (495, 445, 233, 717, 26, 50)])),

def p3_valid(r: int, c: int) -> bool:
    """Same rule as ExamThptProcessor.readPart3Box: row 0 only col 0 ('-'), row 1 cols 1-2 ('.')."""
    return c == 0 if r == 0 else (c in (1, 2) if r == 1 else True)


def cell_name_parts(spec, r, c):
    """(region, position, option) exactly as the app's BubbleDatasetDumper names files."""
    kind = spec["kind"]
    if kind == "grid":
        return spec["region"], f"c{c}", str(r)
    if kind == "answers":
        return spec["region"], f"q{spec['start'] + r}", "ABCD"[c]
    if kind == "tf":
        return "p2", f"q{spec['start'] + r}", "T" if c == 0 else "F"
    option = "neg" if r == 0 else ("dot" if r == 1 else str(r - 2))
    return "p3", f"q{spec['start']}c{c}", option


def cells_of(spec):
    for r in range(spec["rows"]):
        for c in range(spec["cols"]):
            if spec["kind"] != "number" or p3_valid(r, c):
                yield r, c


# ---------------- Same corner detection as ScannerCore.findExamCorners ----------------
def find_corners(gray):
    edges = cv2.Canny(cv2.GaussianBlur(gray, (5, 5), 0), 75, 200)
    contours, _ = cv2.findContours(edges, cv2.RETR_LIST, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
    squares = []
    for cnt in contours:
        approx = cv2.approxPolyDP(cnt.astype(np.float32), 0.03 * cv2.arcLength(cnt, True), True)
        if 4 <= len(approx) <= 6:
            area = cv2.contourArea(approx)
            if 100 <= area <= 30000:
                x, y, w, h = cv2.boundingRect(cnt)
                if 0.5 <= w / h <= 2.0:
                    squares.append((approx, area))
    if len(squares) < 4:
        return None
    median = sorted(a for _, a in squares)[len(squares) // 2]
    centers = []
    for s, a in squares:
        if median * 0.1 <= a <= median * 15:
            x, y, w, h = cv2.boundingRect(s.astype(np.int32))
            centers.append((x + w / 2, y + h / 2))
    if len(centers) < 4:
        return None
    c = np.array(centers)
    tl, br = c[np.argmin(c.sum(1))], c[np.argmax(c.sum(1))]
    tr, bl = c[np.argmax(c[:, 0] - c[:, 1])], c[np.argmin(c[:, 0] - c[:, 1])]
    wt, hl = np.linalg.norm(tr - tl), np.linalg.norm(bl - tl)
    wb, hr = np.linalg.norm(br - bl), np.linalg.norm(br - tr)
    if wt < 80 or hl < 100 or hl < wt * 1.05 or abs(wt - wb) > wt * 0.25 or abs(hl - hr) > hl * 0.25:
        return None
    return np.array([tl, tr, br, bl], dtype=np.float32)


# ---------------- Drawing marks ----------------
def _blob_mask(shape, center, radius, rng, roughness=0.12):
    """Irregular filled shape (hand-made fill), radius varies around the circle."""
    angles = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 40, endpoint=False)
    radii = radius * (1 + rng.normal(0, roughness, angles.size))
    radii = cv2.GaussianBlur(radii.reshape(1, -1).astype(np.float32), (1, 5), 0).ravel()
    pts = np.stack([center[0] + radii * np.cos(angles), center[1] + radii * np.sin(angles)], 1)
    mask = np.zeros(shape, np.uint8)
    cv2.fillPoly(mask, [pts.astype(np.int32)], 255, cv2.LINE_AA)
    return mask


def _paint(img, mask, tone, rng, grain):
    """Darken img towards `tone` where mask is set, with graphite grain texture."""
    m = mask.astype(np.float32) / 255.0
    texture = tone + rng.normal(0, grain, img.shape)
    texture = cv2.GaussianBlur(texture.astype(np.float32), (3, 3), 0)
    out = img.astype(np.float32) * (1 - m) + np.minimum(img.astype(np.float32), texture) * m
    img[:] = np.clip(out, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)


def _strokes(img, center, radius, rng, tone, n, thickness):
    for _ in range(n):
        ang = rng.uniform(0, np.pi)
        off = rng.uniform(-0.6, 0.6) * radius
        dx, dy = np.cos(ang) * radius, np.sin(ang) * radius
        ox, oy = -np.sin(ang) * off, np.cos(ang) * off
        p1 = (int(center[0] - dx + ox), int(center[1] - dy + oy))
        p2 = (int(center[0] + dx + ox), int(center[1] + dy + oy))
        cv2.line(img, p1, p2, float(tone), thickness, cv2.LINE_AA)


def draw_mark(img, center, radius, style, rng):
    cx, cy = center
    jitter = rng.normal(0, radius * 0.08, 2)
    c = (cx + jitter[0], cy + jitter[1])
    if style == "dark":
        _paint(img, _blob_mask(img.shape, c, radius * rng.uniform(0.82, 1.0), rng), rng.uniform(20, 75), rng, 18)
    elif style == "light":
        _paint(img, _blob_mask(img.shape, c, radius * rng.uniform(0.8, 1.0), rng), rng.uniform(105, 165), rng, 22)
    elif style == "partial":   # half-filled, crescent or small dot
        sub = rng.choice(["small", "crescent"])
        if sub == "small":
            mask = _blob_mask(img.shape, c, radius * rng.uniform(0.4, 0.65), rng, 0.15)
        else:
            mask = _blob_mask(img.shape, c, radius * 0.95, rng)
            off = rng.uniform(0.35, 0.7) * radius
            ang = rng.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi)
            cut = _blob_mask(img.shape, (c[0] + off * np.cos(ang), c[1] + off * np.sin(ang)), radius * 0.9, rng)
            mask = cv2.subtract(mask, cut)
        _paint(img, mask, rng.uniform(25, 90), rng, 18)
    elif style == "overflow":  # bigger than the bubble and off-centre
        c2 = (c[0] + rng.uniform(-0.25, 0.25) * radius, c[1] + rng.uniform(-0.25, 0.25) * radius)
        _paint(img, _blob_mask(img.shape, c2, radius * rng.uniform(1.05, 1.3), rng, 0.15), rng.uniform(25, 80), rng, 18)
    elif style == "pen":       # ballpoint: dark, smooth, scribble strokes
        _paint(img, _blob_mask(img.shape, c, radius * rng.uniform(0.8, 0.98), rng, 0.08), rng.uniform(10, 45), rng, 6)
        _strokes(img, c, radius * 0.9, rng, rng.uniform(5, 30), int(rng.integers(2, 5)), 1)
    elif style == "erased":    # graphite left after erasing + eraser streaks
        _paint(img, _blob_mask(img.shape, c, radius * rng.uniform(0.8, 1.05), rng, 0.2), rng.uniform(165, 215), rng, 15)
        _strokes(img, c, radius, rng, rng.uniform(140, 200), int(rng.integers(1, 4)), 1)
    elif style == "x":
        tone, d = rng.uniform(20, 90), radius * rng.uniform(0.7, 1.05)
        t = int(rng.integers(1, 3))
        cv2.line(img, (int(c[0] - d), int(c[1] - d)), (int(c[0] + d), int(c[1] + d)), float(tone), t, cv2.LINE_AA)
        cv2.line(img, (int(c[0] - d), int(c[1] + d)), (int(c[0] + d), int(c[1] - d)), float(tone), t, cv2.LINE_AA)
    elif style == "slash":     # crossed out with one line
        tone, d = rng.uniform(20, 90), radius * rng.uniform(0.8, 1.15)
        ang = rng.uniform(0.5, 1.1)
        cv2.line(img, (int(c[0] - d * np.cos(ang)), int(c[1] + d * np.sin(ang))),
                 (int(c[0] + d * np.cos(ang)), int(c[1] - d * np.sin(ang))), float(tone), int(rng.integers(1, 3)), cv2.LINE_AA)


def filled_style(rng):
    return rng.choice(FILLED_STYLES, p=[0.55, 0.13, 0.12, 0.08, 0.12])


def erased_style(rng):
    return rng.choice(ERASED_STYLES, p=[0.6, 0.25, 0.15])


def plan_marks(layout, template_id, rng):
    """{(spec_index, r, c): style}. Includes realistic mistakes: blanks, double fills, changed answers."""
    marks = {}
    for i, spec in enumerate(layout):
        kind, rows, cols = spec["kind"], spec["rows"], spec["cols"]
        if kind == "grid":  # one digit per column
            for c in range(cols):
                marks[(i, int(rng.integers(rows)), c)] = filled_style(rng) if rng.random() < 0.97 else erased_style(rng)
                if rng.random() < 0.06:  # changed a digit
                    marks.setdefault((i, int(rng.integers(rows)), c), erased_style(rng))
        elif kind in ("answers", "tf"):
            for r in range(rows):
                u = rng.random()
                chosen = [] if u < 0.07 else (list(rng.choice(cols, 2, replace=False)) if u < 0.11
                                              else [int(rng.integers(cols))])
                for c in chosen:
                    marks[(i, r, int(c))] = filled_style(rng)
                if rng.random() < 0.22:  # changed mind on another option
                    others = [c for c in range(cols) if c not in chosen]
                    if others:
                        marks[(i, r, int(rng.choice(others)))] = erased_style(rng)
        else:  # THPT part 3 number: optional sign/decimal point + digits from the left
            n_digits = int(rng.integers(1, 5))
            for c in range(n_digits):
                marks[(i, 2 + int(rng.integers(10)), c)] = filled_style(rng)
            if rng.random() < 0.2:
                marks[(i, 0, 0)] = filled_style(rng)
            if rng.random() < 0.25:
                marks[(i, 1, int(rng.choice([1, 2])))] = filled_style(rng)
            if rng.random() < 0.2:
                r, c = 2 + int(rng.integers(10)), int(rng.integers(4))
                marks.setdefault((i, r, c), erased_style(rng))
    return marks


# ---------------- Photo effects ----------------
def make_photo(page_gray, rng):
    h, w = page_gray.shape
    pad = int(w * rng.uniform(0.05, 0.12))
    desk = np.array([rng.uniform(40, 120), rng.uniform(60, 140), rng.uniform(80, 170)], np.float32)
    canvas = np.empty((h + 2 * pad, w + 2 * pad, 3), np.float32)
    canvas[:] = desk + rng.normal(0, 6, canvas.shape)
    canvas[pad:pad + h, pad:pad + w] = cv2.cvtColor(page_gray, cv2.COLOR_GRAY2BGR)
    H2, W2 = canvas.shape[:2]
    src = np.float32([[0, 0], [W2, 0], [W2, H2], [0, H2]])
    dst = (src + rng.uniform(-0.03, 0.03, src.shape) * [W2, H2]).astype(np.float32)
    canvas = cv2.warpPerspective(canvas, cv2.getPerspectiveTransform(src, dst), (W2, H2), borderMode=cv2.BORDER_REPLICATE)
    # uneven light + colour tint (warm lamp / cool daylight)
    gx = np.linspace(rng.uniform(0.75, 1.0), rng.uniform(0.9, 1.1), W2, dtype=np.float32)[None, :, None]
    gy = np.linspace(rng.uniform(0.85, 1.08), rng.uniform(0.75, 1.0), H2, dtype=np.float32)[:, None, None]
    tint = np.array([rng.uniform(0.85, 1.05), rng.uniform(0.95, 1.03), rng.uniform(0.97, 1.12)], np.float32)
    canvas = canvas * gx * gy * tint
    if rng.random() < 0.5:  # soft shadow (hand / phone)
        mask = np.zeros((H2, W2), np.float32)
        cv2.ellipse(mask, (int(rng.uniform(0, W2)), int(rng.uniform(0, H2))),
                    (int(W2 * rng.uniform(0.2, 0.5)), int(H2 * rng.uniform(0.15, 0.4))), rng.uniform(0, 180), 0, 360, 1, -1)
        mask = cv2.GaussianBlur(mask, (0, 0), W2 * 0.06)
        canvas *= (1 - rng.uniform(0.15, 0.4) * mask)[:, :, None]
    canvas += rng.normal(0, rng.uniform(1.5, 5), canvas.shape)
    photo = np.clip(canvas, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    blur = rng.choice(["none", "gauss", "motion"], p=[0.4, 0.4, 0.2])
    if blur == "gauss":
        photo = cv2.GaussianBlur(photo, (0, 0), rng.uniform(0.6, 1.4))
    elif blur == "motion":
        k = int(rng.integers(3, 6))
        kernel = np.zeros((k, k), np.float32)
        kernel[k // 2, :] = 1.0 / k
        rot = cv2.getRotationMatrix2D((k / 2 - 0.5, k / 2 - 0.5), rng.uniform(0, 180), 1)
        photo = cv2.filter2D(photo, -1, cv2.warpAffine(kernel, rot, (k, k)))
    scale = rng.uniform(0.7, 1.0)  # lower camera resolution
    if scale < 0.98:
        photo = cv2.resize(photo, None, fx=scale, fy=scale, interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
    ok, buf = cv2.imencode(".jpg", photo, [cv2.IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY, int(rng.integers(60, 95))])
    return cv2.imdecode(buf, cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)


# ---------------- Python copy of the app pipeline ----------------
def app_gray(photo_bgr):
    """App: bitmapToMat gives RGBA, then COLOR_BGR2GRAY → R and B weights are swapped. Do the same."""
    return cv2.cvtColor(cv2.cvtColor(photo_bgr, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB), cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)


def run_app_pipeline(photo_bgr, layout):
    gray = app_gray(photo_bgr)
    corners = find_corners(gray)
    if corners is None:
        return None
    m = cv2.getPerspectiveTransform(corners, np.float32([[0, 0], [W, 0], [W, H], [0, H]]))
    warped = cv2.warpPerspective(gray, m, (int(W), int(H)))
    binary = cv2.adaptiveThreshold(warped, 255, cv2.ADAPTIVE_THRESH_GAUSSIAN_C, cv2.THRESH_BINARY_INV, 51, 10)
    cells = []
    for i, spec in enumerate(layout):
        x, y, w, h = spec["roi"]
        cw, ch = w / spec["cols"], h / spec["rows"]
        radius = int(min(cw, ch) * spec["r"])
        mask = np.zeros((int(ch), int(cw)), np.uint8)
        cv2.circle(mask, (int(round(cw / 2)), int(round(ch / 2))), radius, 255, -1)
        for r, c in cells_of(spec):
            rx, ry = x + int(c * cw), y + int(r * ch)
            cell_bin = binary[ry:ry + int(ch), rx:rx + int(cw)]
            filled = cv2.countNonZero(cv2.bitwise_and(cell_bin, mask[:cell_bin.shape[0], :cell_bin.shape[1]])) \
                > np.pi * radius * radius * 0.5
            cells.append((i, r, c, filled, warped[ry:ry + int(ch), rx:rx + int(cw)].copy()))
    return cells


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--raw", default=str(DEFAULT_RAW), help="folder with the app's form_*.pdf templates")
    ap.add_argument("--per-template", type=int, default=12)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=2026)
    ap.add_argument("--tag", default="v1")
    ap.add_argument("--sample-photos", type=int, default=1, help="photos to keep per template for viewing")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    rng = np.random.default_rng(args.seed)
    out = Path(args.out)
    (out / "photos").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    zip_path = out / f"bubble_dataset_synth_{args.tag}.zip"
    labels, stats, skipped = {}, Counter(), 0

    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, "w", zipfile.ZIP_STORED) as zf:  # PNGs are already compressed
        for template_id, (stem, layout) in sorted(LAYOUTS.items()):
            pix = fitz.open(Path(args.raw) / f"{stem}.pdf")[0].get_pixmap(dpi=200)
            base = np.frombuffer(pix.samples, np.uint8).reshape(pix.height, pix.width, pix.n)
            base = cv2.cvtColor(base, cv2.COLOR_RGB2GRAY if pix.n == 3 else cv2.COLOR_RGBA2GRAY)
            corners = find_corners(base)
            to_page = cv2.getPerspectiveTransform(np.float32([[0, 0], [W, 0], [W, H], [0, H]]), corners)
            scale = np.linalg.norm(corners[1] - corners[0]) / W

            for n in range(args.per_template):
                page = base.copy()
                marks = plan_marks(layout, template_id, rng)
                for (i, r, c), style in marks.items():
                    spec = layout[i]
                    x, y, w, h = spec["roi"]
                    cw, ch = w / spec["cols"], h / spec["rows"]
                    wx, wy = x + (c + 0.5) * cw, y + (r + 0.5) * ch
                    px, py = cv2.perspectiveTransform(np.float32([[[wx, wy]]]), to_page)[0, 0]
                    draw_mark(page, (px, py), min(cw, ch) * spec["r"] * scale, style, rng)
                photo = make_photo(page, rng)
                cells = run_app_pipeline(photo, layout)
                if cells is None:
                    skipped += 1
                    continue
                if n < args.sample_photos:
                    cv2.imwrite(str(out / "photos" / f"synth_t{template_id}_{stem[5:]}_{n + 1}.jpg"), photo)
                sheet_id = f"990101-{template_id}{n:05d}-syn{args.seed % 1000:03d}"
                for i, r, c, filled, crop in cells:
                    region, position, option = cell_name_parts(layout[i], r, c)
                    name = f"{sheet_id}_t{template_id}_{region}_{position}_{option}.png"
                    auto = "filled" if filled else "empty"
                    style = marks.get((i, r, c))
                    truth = "empty" if style is None else ("erased" if style in ERASED_STYLES else "filled")
                    zf.writestr(f"bubble_dataset/{auto}/{name}", cv2.imencode(".png", crop)[1].tobytes())
                    labels[name] = truth
                    stats[(truth, auto)] += 1
                    if style:
                        stats[("style", style, auto)] += 1

    with (out / "labels_override.csv").open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f)
        writer.writerow(["filename", "label"])
        writer.writerows(sorted(labels.items()))

    total = sum(v for k, v in stats.items() if k[0] != "style")
    lines = [f"Sheets: {args.per_template * len(LAYOUTS) - skipped} made, {skipped} skipped (app could not find corners)",
             f"Cells: {total}"]
    for truth in ("empty", "filled", "erased"):
        n_all = stats[(truth, "empty")] + stats[(truth, "filled")]
        wrong = stats[(truth, "empty")] if truth == "filled" else stats[(truth, "filled")]
        lines.append(f"  {truth:>6}: {n_all:6d} cells — old 50% rule wrong on {wrong} ({wrong / max(n_all, 1):.1%})")
    lines.append("Old rule by mark style (cells read as 'filled' / total):")
    for style in FILLED_STYLES + ERASED_STYLES:
        f_, e_ = stats[("style", style, "filled")], stats[("style", style, "empty")]
        lines.append(f"  {style:>8}: {f_}/{f_ + e_}")
    report = "\n".join(lines)
    (out / "stats.txt").write_text(report + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(report)
    print(f"\nWrote {zip_path} ({zip_path.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB) and {out / 'labels_override.csv'}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Make a COMPUTER-MADE training dataset in exactly the format the QuizMark app exports.

Steps for every sheet:
  1. Render a template PDF from the app (QuizMark/app/src/main/res/raw/form_*.pdf).
  2. Draw marks exactly on the cells the app reads (ROI coordinates copied from the app's
     util/scanner/*Processor.kt, mapped through the same 4 corner markers ScannerCore uses).
     Mark styles: dark / light / partial / overflowing pencil, pen, erased, X, single slash.
  3. Add photo effects: desk border, perspective, uneven light, shadow, colour tint, blur,
     noise, lower resolution, JPEG compression.
  4. Run a Python copy of the app pipeline (corner detection → 800x1200 warp → adaptive
     threshold → 50% rule) and cut every cell from the warped gray image, like BubbleDatasetDumper.

Outputs (in --out):
  bubble_dataset_synth_<tag>.zip  → upload to  My Drive/quizmark-ml/data/
  labels_override.csv             → upload to  My Drive/quizmark-ml/   (TRUE labels incl. "erased")
  photos/                         → a few sample sheet photos to look at
  stats.txt                       → what the old 50% rule gets wrong on this data

This is practice data. A model trained only on it must not be shipped before it is trained on real sheets.

Usage (needs: numpy, opencv-python, pymupdf):
  python tools/make_sheet_dataset.py --out ../quizmark-synthetic --per-template 12 --seed 2026
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import io
import zipfile
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

import cv2
import fitz  # pymupdf
import numpy as np

DEFAULT_RAW = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "QuizMark" / "app" / "src" / "main" / "res" / "raw"
W, H = 800.0, 1200.0
FILLED_STYLES = ("dark", "light", "partial", "overflow", "pen")
ERASED_STYLES = ("erased", "x", "slash")

def p3_valid(r: int, c: int) -> bool:
    """Same rule as ExamThptProcessor.readPart3Box: row 0 only col 0 ('-'), row 1 cols 1-2 ('.')."""
    return c == 0 if r == 0 else (c in (1, 2) if r == 1 else True)


def cell_name_parts(spec, r, c):
    """(region, position, option) exactly as the app's BubbleDatasetDumper names files."""
    kind = spec["kind"]
    if kind == "grid":
        return spec["region"], f"c{c}", str(r)
    if kind == "answers":
        return spec["region"], f"q{spec['start'] + r}", "ABCD"[c]
    if kind == "tf":
        return "p2", f"q{spec['start'] + r}", "T" if c == 0 else "F"
    option = "neg" if r == 0 else ("dot" if r == 1 else str(r - 2))
    return "p3", f"q{spec['start']}c{c}", option


def cells_of(spec):
    for r in range(spec["rows"]):
        for c in range(spec["cols"]):
            if spec["kind"] != "number" or p3_valid(r, c):
                yield r, c


# ---------------- Same corner detection as ScannerCore.findExamCorners ----------------
def find_corners(gray):
    edges = cv2.Canny(cv2.GaussianBlur(gray, (5, 5), 0), 75, 200)
    contours, _ = cv2.findContours(edges, cv2.RETR_LIST, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
    squares = []
    for cnt in contours:
        approx = cv2.approxPolyDP(cnt.astype(np.float32), 0.03 * cv2.arcLength(cnt, True), True)
        if 4 <= len(approx) <= 6:
            area = cv2.contourArea(approx)
            if 100 <= area <= 30000:
                x, y, w, h = cv2.boundingRect(cnt)
                if 0.5 <= w / h <= 2.0:
                    squares.append((approx, area))
    if len(squares) < 4:
        return None
    median = sorted(a for _, a in squares)[len(squares) // 2]
    centers = []
    for s, a in squares:
        if median * 0.1 <= a <= median * 15:
            x, y, w, h = cv2.boundingRect(s.astype(np.int32))
            centers.append((x + w / 2, y + h / 2))
    if len(centers) < 4:
        return None
    c = np.array(centers)
    tl, br = c[np.argmin(c.sum(1))], c[np.argmax(c.sum(1))]
    tr, bl = c[np.argmax(c[:, 0] - c[:, 1])], c[np.argmin(c[:, 0] - c[:, 1])]
    wt, hl = np.linalg.norm(tr - tl), np.linalg.norm(bl - tl)
    wb, hr = np.linalg.norm(br - bl), np.linalg.norm(br - tr)
    if wt < 80 or hl < 100 or hl < wt * 1.05 or abs(wt - wb) > wt * 0.25 or abs(hl - hr) > hl * 0.25:
        return None
    return np.array([tl, tr, br, bl], dtype=np.float32)


# ---------------- Drawing marks ----------------
def _blob_mask(shape, center, radius, rng, roughness=0.12):
    """Irregular filled shape (hand-made fill), radius varies around the circle."""
    angles = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 40, endpoint=False)
    radii = radius * (1 + rng.normal(0, roughness, angles.size))
    radii = cv2.GaussianBlur(radii.reshape(1, -1).astype(np.float32), (1, 5), 0).ravel()
    pts = np.stack([center[0] + radii * np.cos(angles), center[1] + radii * np.sin(angles)], 1)
    mask = np.zeros(shape, np.uint8)
    cv2.fillPoly(mask, [pts.astype(np.int32)], 255, cv2.LINE_AA)
    return mask


def _paint(img, mask, tone, rng, grain):
    """Darken img towards `tone` where mask is set, with graphite grain texture."""
    m = mask.astype(np.float32) / 255.0
    texture = tone + rng.normal(0, grain, img.shape)
    texture = cv2.GaussianBlur(texture.astype(np.float32), (3, 3), 0)
    out = img.astype(np.float32) * (1 - m) + np.minimum(img.astype(np.float32), texture) * m
    img[:] = np.clip(out, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)


def _strokes(img, center, radius, rng, tone, n, thickness):
    for _ in range(n):
        ang = rng.uniform(0, np.pi)
        off = rng.uniform(-0.6, 0.6) * radius
        dx, dy = np.cos(ang) * radius, np.sin(ang) * radius
        ox, oy = -np.sin(ang) * off, np.cos(ang) * off
        p1 = (int(center[0] - dx + ox), int(center[1] - dy + oy))
        p2 = (int(center[0] + dx + ox), int(center[1] + dy + oy))
        cv2.line(img, p1, p2, float(tone), thickness, cv2.LINE_AA)


def draw_mark(img, center, radius, style, rng):
    cx, cy = center
    jitter = rng.normal(0, radius * 0.08, 2)
    c = (cx + jitter[0], cy + jitter[1])
    if style == "dark":
        _paint(img, _blob_mask(img.shape, c, radius * rng.uniform(0.82, 1.0), rng), rng.uniform(20, 75), rng, 18)
    elif style == "light":
        _paint(img, _blob_mask(img.shape, c, radius * rng.uniform(0.8, 1.0), rng), rng.uniform(105, 165), rng, 22)
    elif style == "partial":   # half-filled, crescent or small dot
        sub = rng.choice(["small", "crescent"])
        if sub == "small":
            mask = _blob_mask(img.shape, c, radius * rng.uniform(0.4, 0.65), rng, 0.15)
        else:
            mask = _blob_mask(img.shape, c, radius * 0.95, rng)
            off = rng.uniform(0.35, 0.7) * radius
            ang = rng.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi)
            cut = _blob_mask(img.shape, (c[0] + off * np.cos(ang), c[1] + off * np.sin(ang)), radius * 0.9, rng)
            mask = cv2.subtract(mask, cut)
        _paint(img, mask, rng.uniform(25, 90), rng, 18)
    elif style == "overflow":  # bigger than the bubble and off-centre
        c2 = (c[0] + rng.uniform(-0.25, 0.25) * radius, c[1] + rng.uniform(-0.25, 0.25) * radius)
        _paint(img, _blob_mask(img.shape, c2, radius * rng.uniform(1.05, 1.3), rng, 0.15), rng.uniform(25, 80), rng, 18)
    elif style == "pen":       # ballpoint: dark, smooth, scribble strokes
        _paint(img, _blob_mask(img.shape, c, radius * rng.uniform(0.8, 0.98), rng, 0.08), rng.uniform(10, 45), rng, 6)
        _strokes(img, c, radius * 0.9, rng, rng.uniform(5, 30), int(rng.integers(2, 5)), 1)
    elif style == "erased":    # graphite left after erasing + eraser streaks
        _paint(img, _blob_mask(img.shape, c, radius * rng.uniform(0.8, 1.05), rng, 0.2), rng.uniform(165, 215), rng, 15)
        _strokes(img, c, radius, rng, rng.uniform(140, 200), int(rng.integers(1, 4)), 1)
    elif style == "x":
        tone, d = rng.uniform(20, 90), radius * rng.uniform(0.7, 1.05)
        t = int(rng.integers(1, 3))
        cv2.line(img, (int(c[0] - d), int(c[1] - d)), (int(c[0] + d), int(c[1] + d)), float(tone), t, cv2.LINE_AA)
        cv2.line(img, (int(c[0] - d), int(c[1] + d)), (int(c[0] + d), int(c[1] - d)), float(tone), t, cv2.LINE_AA)
    elif style == "slash":     # crossed out with one line
        tone, d = rng.uniform(20, 90), radius * rng.uniform(0.8, 1.15)
        ang = rng.uniform(0.5, 1.1)
        cv2.line(img, (int(c[0] - d * np.cos(ang)), int(c[1] + d * np.sin(ang))),
                 (int(c[0] + d * np.cos(ang)), int(c[1] - d * np.sin(ang))), float(tone), int(rng.integers(1, 3)), cv2.LINE_AA)


def filled_style(rng):
    return rng.choice(FILLED_STYLES, p=[0.55, 0.13, 0.12, 0.08, 0.12])


def erased_style(rng):
    return rng.choice(ERASED_STYLES, p=[0.6, 0.25, 0.15])


def plan_marks(layout, template_id, rng):
    """{(spec_index, r, c): style}. Includes realistic mistakes: blanks, double fills, changed answers."""
    marks = {}
    for i, spec in enumerate(layout):
        kind, rows, cols = spec["kind"], spec["rows"], spec["cols"]
        if kind == "grid":  # one digit per column
            for c in range(cols):
                marks[(i, int(rng.integers(rows)), c)] = filled_style(rng) if rng.random() < 0.97 else erased_style(rng)
                if rng.random() < 0.06:  # changed a digit
                    marks.setdefault((i, int(rng.integers(rows)), c), erased_style(rng))
        elif kind in ("answers", "tf"):
            for r in range(rows):
                u = rng.random()
                chosen = [] if u < 0.07 else (list(rng.choice(cols, 2, replace=False)) if u < 0.11
                                              else [int(rng.integers(cols))])
                for c in chosen:
                    marks[(i, r, int(c))] = filled_style(rng)
                if rng.random() < 0.22:  # changed mind on another option
                    others = [c for c in range(cols) if c not in chosen]
                    if others:
                        marks[(i, r, int(rng.choice(others)))] = erased_style(rng)
        else:  # THPT part 3 number: optional sign/decimal point + digits from the left
            n_digits = int(rng.integers(1, 5))
            for c in range(n_digits):
                marks[(i, 2 + int(rng.integers(10)), c)] = filled_style(rng)
            if rng.random() < 0.2:
                marks[(i, 0, 0)] = filled_style(rng)
            if rng.random() < 0.25:
                marks[(i, 1, int(rng.choice([1, 2])))] = filled_style(rng)
            if rng.random() < 0.2:
                r, c = 2 + int(rng.integers(10)), int(rng.integers(4))
                marks.setdefault((i, r, c), erased_style(rng))
    return marks


# ---------------- Photo effects ----------------
def make_photo(page_gray, rng):
    h, w = page_gray.shape
    pad = int(w * rng.uniform(0.05, 0.12))
    desk = np.array([rng.uniform(40, 120), rng.uniform(60, 140), rng.uniform(80, 170)], np.float32)
    canvas = np.empty((h + 2 * pad, w + 2 * pad, 3), np.float32)
    canvas[:] = desk + rng.normal(0, 6, canvas.shape)
    canvas[pad:pad + h, pad:pad + w] = cv2.cvtColor(page_gray, cv2.COLOR_GRAY2BGR)
    H2, W2 = canvas.shape[:2]
    src = np.float32([[0, 0], [W2, 0], [W2, H2], [0, H2]])
    dst = (src + rng.uniform(-0.03, 0.03, src.shape) * [W2, H2]).astype(np.float32)
    canvas = cv2.warpPerspective(canvas, cv2.getPerspectiveTransform(src, dst), (W2, H2), borderMode=cv2.BORDER_REPLICATE)
    # uneven light + colour tint (warm lamp / cool daylight)
    gx = np.linspace(rng.uniform(0.75, 1.0), rng.uniform(0.9, 1.1), W2, dtype=np.float32)[None, :, None]
    gy = np.linspace(rng.uniform(0.85, 1.08), rng.uniform(0.75, 1.0), H2, dtype=np.float32)[:, None, None]
    tint = np.array([rng.uniform(0.85, 1.05), rng.uniform(0.95, 1.03), rng.uniform(0.97, 1.12)], np.float32)
    canvas = canvas * gx * gy * tint
    if rng.random() < 0.5:  # soft shadow (hand / phone)
        mask = np.zeros((H2, W2), np.float32)
        cv2.ellipse(mask, (int(rng.uniform(0, W2)), int(rng.uniform(0, H2))),
                    (int(W2 * rng.uniform(0.2, 0.5)), int(H2 * rng.uniform(0.15, 0.4))), rng.uniform(0, 180), 0, 360, 1, -1)
        mask = cv2.GaussianBlur(mask, (0, 0), W2 * 0.06)
        canvas *= (1 - rng.uniform(0.15, 0.4) * mask)[:, :, None]
    canvas += rng.normal(0, rng.uniform(1.5, 5), canvas.shape)
    photo = np.clip(canvas, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    blur = rng.choice(["none", "gauss", "motion"], p=[0.4, 0.4, 0.2])
    if blur == "gauss":
        photo = cv2.GaussianBlur(photo, (0, 0), rng.uniform(0.6, 1.4))
    elif blur == "motion":
        k = int(rng.integers(3, 6))
        kernel = np.zeros((k, k), np.float32)
        kernel[k // 2, :] = 1.0 / k
        rot = cv2.getRotationMatrix2D((k / 2 - 0.5, k / 2 - 0.5), rng.uniform(0, 180), 1)
        photo = cv2.filter2D(photo, -1, cv2.warpAffine(kernel, rot, (k, k)))
    scale = rng.uniform(0.7, 1.0)  # lower camera resolution
    if scale < 0.98:
        photo = cv2.resize(photo, None, fx=scale, fy=scale, interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
    ok, buf = cv2.imencode(".jpg", photo, [cv2.IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY, int(rng.integers(60, 95))])
    return cv2.imdecode(buf, cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)


# ---------------- Python copy of the app pipeline ----------------
def app_gray(photo_bgr):
    """App: bitmapToMat gives RGBA, then COLOR_BGR2GRAY → R and B weights are swapped. Do the same."""
    return cv2.cvtColor(cv2.cvtColor(photo_bgr, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB), cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)


def run_app_pipeline(photo_bgr, layout):
    gray = app_gray(photo_bgr)
    corners = find_corners(gray)
    if corners is None:
        return None
    m = cv2.getPerspectiveTransform(corners, np.float32([[0, 0], [W, 0], [W, H], [0, H]]))
    warped = cv2.warpPerspective(gray, m, (int(W), int(H)))
    binary = cv2.adaptiveThreshold(warped, 255, cv2.ADAPTIVE_THRESH_GAUSSIAN_C, cv2.THRESH_BINARY_INV, 51, 10)
    cells = []
    for i, spec in enumerate(layout):
        x, y, w, h = spec["roi"]
        cw, ch = w / spec["cols"], h / spec["rows"]
        radius = int(min(cw, ch) * spec["r"])
        mask = np.zeros((int(ch), int(cw)), np.uint8)
        cv2.circle(mask, (int(round(cw / 2)), int(round(ch / 2))), radius, 255, -1)
        for r, c in cells_of(spec):
            rx, ry = x + int(c * cw), y + int(r * ch)
            cell_bin = binary[ry:ry + int(ch), rx:rx + int(cw)]
            filled = cv2.countNonZero(cv2.bitwise_and(cell_bin, mask[:cell_bin.shape[0], :cell_bin.shape[1]])) \
                > np.pi * radius * radius * 0.5
            cells.append((i, r, c, filled, warped[ry:ry + int(ch), rx:rx + int(cw)].copy()))
    return cells


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--raw", default=str(DEFAULT_RAW), help="folder with the app's form_*.pdf templates")
    ap.add_argument("--per-template", type=int, default=12)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=2026)
    ap.add_argument("--tag", default="v1")
    ap.add_argument("--sample-photos", type=int, default=1, help="photos to keep per template for viewing")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    rng = np.random.default_rng(args.seed)
    out = Path(args.out)
    (out / "photos").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    zip_path = out / f"bubble_dataset_synth_{args.tag}.zip"
    labels, stats, skipped = {}, Counter(), 0

    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, "w", zipfile.ZIP_STORED) as zf:  # PNGs are already compressed
        for template_id, (stem, layout) in sorted(LAYOUTS.items()):
            pix = fitz.open(Path(args.raw) / f"{stem}.pdf")[0].get_pixmap(dpi=200)
            base = np.frombuffer(pix.samples, np.uint8).reshape(pix.height, pix.width, pix.n)
            base = cv2.cvtColor(base, cv2.COLOR_RGB2GRAY if pix.n == 3 else cv2.COLOR_RGBA2GRAY)
            corners = find_corners(base)
            to_page = cv2.getPerspectiveTransform(np.float32([[0, 0], [W, 0], [W, H], [0, H]]), corners)
            scale = np.linalg.norm(corners[1] - corners[0]) / W

            for n in range(args.per_template):
                page = base.copy()
                marks = plan_marks(layout, template_id, rng)
                for (i, r, c), style in marks.items():
                    spec = layout[i]
                    x, y, w, h = spec["roi"]
                    cw, ch = w / spec["cols"], h / spec["rows"]
                    wx, wy = x + (c + 0.5) * cw, y + (r + 0.5) * ch
                    px, py = cv2.perspectiveTransform(np.float32([[[wx, wy]]]), to_page)[0, 0]
                    draw_mark(page, (px, py), min(cw, ch) * spec["r"] * scale, style, rng)
                photo = make_photo(page, rng)
                cells = run_app_pipeline(photo, layout)
                if cells is None:
                    skipped += 1
                    continue
                if n < args.sample_photos:
                    cv2.imwrite(str(out / "photos" / f"synth_t{template_id}_{stem[5:]}_{n + 1}.jpg"), photo)
                sheet_id = f"990101-{template_id}{n:05d}-syn{args.seed % 1000:03d}"
                for i, r, c, filled, crop in cells:
                    region, position, option = cell_name_parts(layout[i], r, c)
                    name = f"{sheet_id}_t{template_id}_{region}_{position}_{option}.png"
                    auto = "filled" if filled else "empty"
                    style = marks.get((i, r, c))
                    truth = "empty" if style is None else ("erased" if style in ERASED_STYLES else "filled")
                    zf.writestr(f"bubble_dataset/{auto}/{name}", cv2.imencode(".png", crop)[1].tobytes())
                    labels[name] = truth
                    stats[(truth, auto)] += 1
                    if style:
                        stats[("style", style, auto)] += 1

    with (out / "labels_override.csv").open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f)
        writer.writerow(["filename", "label"])
        writer.writerows(sorted(labels.items()))

    total = sum(v for k, v in stats.items() if k[0] != "style")
    lines = [f"Sheets: {args.per_template * len(LAYOUTS) - skipped} made, {skipped} skipped (app could not find corners)",
             f"Cells: {total}"]
    for truth in ("empty", "filled", "erased"):
        n_all = stats[(truth, "empty")] + stats[(truth, "filled")]
        wrong = stats[(truth, "empty")] if truth == "filled" else stats[(truth, "filled")]
        lines.append(f"  {truth:>6}: {n_all:6d} cells — old 50% rule wrong on {wrong} ({wrong / max(n_all, 1):.1%})")
    lines.append("Old rule by mark style (cells read as 'filled' / total):")
    for style in FILLED_STYLES + ERASED_STYLES:
        f_, e_ = stats[("style", style, "filled")], stats[("style", style, "empty")]
        lines.append(f"  {style:>8}: {f_}/{f_ + e_}")
    report = "\n".join(lines)
    (out / "stats.txt").write_text(report + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(report)
    print(f"\nWrote {zip_path} ({zip_path.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB) and {out / 'labels_override.csv'}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - Original: "i want to incorporate AI into this project, how can I do that?" (QuizMark Android app).
   - The direction evolved:
     - First plan: Claude Opus 5.5 grading template 6 via Firebase Cloud Functions (Part A), plus a self-trained bubble classifier (Part B).
     - Then Part A was dropped: there is no budget, the Firebase project `quizmark-fa1de` belongs to someone else, Gemini's free tier is limited, and Google AI Pro doesn't cover API calls.
     - **Current direction: only train their own small CNN** (empty/filled/erased) to replace the fixed 50% threshold in templates 1–5. It runs offline in the app via OpenCV 4.5.3 DNN (ONNX opset 11).
     - Training code lives in a separate repo `quizmark-ml`; training runs on Google Colab Pro; data and labels are kept on Google Drive under `My Drive/quizmark-ml/`.
   - User instructions:
     - "guide me step by step… when it comes to code, you code".
     - **Answer every question in intermediate-level English** (saved to memory). A one-time Vietnamese reply was given when explicitly asked.
     - The user installs on a real Xiaomi Redmi Note 13 Pro over Wi-Fi from **VS Code only (no Android Studio)**.
   - Most recent request: "so what's we here now we need to real data? I haven't data from my phone, can you create for me image and then I will test my model?"

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - App stack: Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Hilt, Firebase Auth/Firestore, CameraX, OpenCV `com.quickbirdstudios:opencv:4.5.3.0` (includes `org.opencv.dnn`).
   - App pipeline:
     - `ScannerCore.findExamCorners`: square contours, area 100–30000, median filter; picks the 4 extreme centers TL=min(x+y), BR=max(x+y), TR=max(x−y), BL=min(x−y), then warps to 800×1200.
     - Processors: adaptiveThreshold (51, 10), then a 50% filled rule per ROI cell.
   - Android 15+ edge-to-edge with 3-button navigation → need `navigationBarsPadding()`. Per-app locale via `AppCompatDelegate`.
   - ML:
     - BubbleNet CNN (~26.5K params).
     - Input: gray cell → 32×32 INTER_AREA → /255, shape [1,1,32,32]. Classes `("empty","filled","erased")`.
     - Split by sheetId; class weights 1/sqrt(n); OneCycleLR, AdamW, macro-F1 model selection.
     - ONNX export: legacy TorchScript (`dynamo=False`, opset 11) with a manual-builder fallback (BN folded into Conv, IR version 6).
     - Verification with OpenCV 4.5.3 in a Python 3.9 venv created by `uv`.
   - Synthetic data generation:
     - Template PDFs are rendered with pymupdf.
     - Marks are drawn on the app's ROI cells, mapped via the corner markers.
     - Photo effects are added, then a Python port of the app pipeline cuts the cells, with a corner-correctness check.
   - adb wireless debugging (`adb pair` / `adb connect`), `adb install -r -t`, Xiaomi "Install via USB" requirement, signature mismatch.

3. Files and Code Sections:

   **QuizMark app (C:\Users\Huong PC\Documents\QuizMark).** All committed by the user: `19fd570`, `c7573bb` (OAuth client/google-services, likely SHA-1), `0c08090`.

     - `Session.save(gray: Mat, cellRect: Rect, region, position, option, isFilled)` writes `filesDir/bubble_dataset/<filled|empty>/<sheetId>_t<template>_<region>_<position>_<option>.png` via `Imgcodecs.imwrite`, inside a try/catch.

   - **The 5 processors** (`Exam20/40/50/120Processor.kt`, `ExamThptProcessor.kt`):
     - `val dump = BubbleDatasetDumper.beginSheet(templateId = N)` at the start of `process()` (THPT=1, 20=2, 40=3, 50=4, 120=5).

# Plan: Đưa AI vào QuizMark — (A) Claude chấm mẫu 6, (B) model tự train phân loại ô tô cho mẫu 1–5

## Bối cảnh

QuizMark chấm phiếu trắc nghiệm giấy bằng OpenCV, nhưng hiện có hai điểm yếu.

1. **Mẫu 6 "Phiếu khác (Chấm bằng AI)" mới làm dở.**
   - Đã tạo được đề và nhập đáp án.
   - Nút chụp trong `ManualCaptureCameraScreen.kt:255` vẫn là `// TODO`.
   - Chấm từ thư viện ảnh bị ngầm chuyển sang `Exam20Processor` (`BatchGradingViewModel.kt:62-69`).
2. **Mẫu 1–5 quyết định ô có được tô hay không bằng một ngưỡng cố định**: `Core.countNonZero(maskedCell) > circleArea * 0.50`.
   - Dòng này lặp lại 12 lần trong 5 file `util/scanner/*Processor.kt`.
   - Nó dễ sai khi bút chì nhạt, tẩy không sạch, hoặc phiếu bị bóng hay tối.

**Quyết định của người dùng:**
- Làm **cả hai** phần.
  - **Phần A:** Claude Opus 5.5 đọc phiếu bất kỳ cho mẫu 6, gọi qua Firebase Cloud Functions để giữ API key trên server.
  - **Phần B:** tự train một CNN nhỏ phân loại ô (trống / tô / tẩy) cho mẫu 1–5. Model chạy offline bằng OpenCV DNN.
- Code train đặt ở **repo riêng** `quizmark-ml`.

Hai phần độc lập với nhau. Train model chạy trên **Google Colab Pro** của người dùng.

> **Cập nhật 2026-11-08 (lần 2):** người dùng quyết định **chỉ tự train model, không gọi API AI của bất kỳ bên nào**.
> - Lý do: gói Google AI Pro không kèm quyền gọi Gemini API miễn phí từ app. Quota của gói chỉ dùng trong giao diện web AI Studio. Credit API đi kèm thì phải gắn thanh toán và nạp trước 5 USD.
> - Phần A coi như **bỏ**, trừ khi người dùng đổi ý.
> - Mẫu 6: ở B3 phải xử lý chỗ chấm từ thư viện bị ngầm dùng `Exam20Processor`. Việc ẩn hoặc tắt mẫu 6 trong app sẽ hỏi người dùng sau.
>
> **Cập nhật 2026-11-08:** người dùng chọn **làm Phần B trước, Phần A tạm hoãn**. Lý do: API Claude tốn phí, và Firebase `quizmark-fa1de` thuộc người khác nên không tự nâng Blaze được. Nếu sau này làm lại Phần A, có thể dùng Cloudflare Workers miễn phí thay cho Firebase Functions. Bỏ qua bước 3, 4, 5 trong bảng dưới.

> **Tiến độ:**
> - ✅ Bước 1 (thu dữ liệu trong app; đã biên dịch, chưa commit).
> - ✅ Bước 6: repo `C:\Users\Huong PC\Documents\quizmark-ml`, commit `b95b7e7`.
>   - Đã chạy thử đầu-cuối trên máy bằng dữ liệu giả.
>   - Cả hai cách export đều qua kiểm tra bằng OpenCV 4.5.3 (sai khác khoảng 2e-6).
> - ⏳ Bước 7: chờ người dùng tạo repo GitHub.

## Lộ trình thực hiện (ai làm gì)

Thu dữ liệu tốn thời gian nhất, nên làm B1 trước. Trong lúc bạn tô và quét phiếu, tôi làm Phần A.

| Bước | Việc | Ai làm |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Code B1: chế độ thu dữ liệu ô tô + nút xuất zip (chỉ ở bản debug) | Claude |
| 2 | In phiếu mẫu 1–5, tô đa dạng, quét bằng bản debug, xuất zip lên Google Drive | Bạn |
| 3 | Chuẩn bị Phần A: tạo API key ở console.anthropic.com; nâng Firebase lên Blaze và đặt cảnh báo ngân sách; `npm i -g firebase-tools`; `firebase login` | Bạn |
| 4 | Code Phần A (`functions/` + Android) | Claude |
